Our annual contract is up for renewal on 2027-01-15, and after the pilot run in Q3 the product team wants to double our reserved capacity to support heavier inference loads. We currently run an 8-GPU reserved pool with Redwood and would like to discuss moving to 16 GPUs, updated monthly commit, and an activation cadence that avoids a hard cutover during Black Friday prep.

Hi Asha — great to hear from you and congrats on the successful pilot.

We can absolutely support a staged expansion to 16 GPUs with an activation plan that minimizes risk for OmniRetail during peak season. High-level approach below; I'll follow up with a formal amendment and pricing by COB Friday.

Proposed path (short):
- Term: extend current contract by +6 months (new term ends 2028-07-15) to enable a lower blended monthly rate; open to an 18-month commitment if you want a deeper discount
- Monthly commit: move from current 8-GPU equivalent commit to a 16-GPU equivalent commit; billing will show as a single reserved pool line-item, with phased activation billing pro-rated for first month
- Activation: enable 8 additional GPUs in two 1-week waves starting Feb 1; we’ll run traffic shift canaries and rollback hooks
- Throughput SLA: offer a throughput guidance with a 99th latency escalation path; we can add a throughput SLO and a small credit if we miss the agreed guardrail (details in amendment)

Attachments: I’ve attached a short term sheet (redwood_draft_term_sheet_v1.pdf) with numbers and options. Two asks from our side to firm pricing: final committed term (12 vs 18 months) and a 12-month forecast of peak RPS per shard.

I’ll include Marissa (solutions/ops) and Laura (revops) on the finance/billing and ops coordination.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Hello Asha / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clear forecast and timeline. Attached is a formal amendment (redwood_amendment_16gpu_v2.pdf) including two pricing paths: 12-month and 18-month commitments. Summary highlights below: 

Summary (proposal):
- New monthly reserved commitment: 16-GPU equivalent (billed as reserved pool units)
- Activation cadence: Feb 1 — enable +4 GPUs (canary), Feb 8 — enable +4 GPUs (full staging)
- Billing: Feb month prorated for active GPUs; monthly commit applies starting Feb invoice cycle
- Pricing: 12-month option = $UNIT_A per GPU-month; 18-month option = $UNIT_B per GPU-month (UNIT_B ~= UNIT_A - 9%)
- Throughput/SLO: target 2.5x current baseline; 99th latency objective with a 2% credit of monthly invoice if missed more than 2 calendar days in a month (exclusions: customer traffic spikes outside forecasted range)
- Ops guarantees: warm KV caching, prefix caching layer and dedicated routing to reduce cold-start latencies during ramp

Next steps we propose:
1) You pick 12- or 18-month path and confirm activation window (we can shift start to Feb 7 if you prefer)
2) Procurement to confirm PO timing; we’ll provide a fully executed DocuSign link for amendment once commercial terms are agreed
3) Marissa to run a technical readiness checklist with Devon and provide runbook to OmniRetail 2 weeks before activation

I’ve added the DocuSign link to the amendment in the footer of the attached doc. If procurement needs any security language for Crawford, we can include a short appendix on data isolation and audit logging.

Best,
Vivek
